summary: INSERT INTO adds new rows to a table. You name the columns you are filling and give one set of values per row.
notes: Separate several rows with commas after VALUES to insert them in one statement.
Columns you leave out get NULL (or their DEFAULT). The result shows NULL in those cells.
The id column is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, so SQLite numbered the rows 1, 2, 3.
pitfall: If the number of values does not match the number of columns, nothing is inserted: Parse error: 2 values for 3 columns.
